fact_check.claim: New students ride TCAT free for their first year with the Cornell ID card
fact_check.note: Page says new students ride free for their first year using their Cornell ID card.

fact_check.claim: Eligible: first-year undergraduates, graduate and Ph.D. students in their first year, and first-year transfers
fact_check.note: Page says fully subsidized passes go to students new to their program, including first-year transfers. It does not list 'first-year undergraduates' or 'graduate and Ph.D.' separately; the article's list is paraphrased beyond the source.

fact_check.claim: TCAT passes expire August 31 for fall entrants and December 31 for spring entrants
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: After the first year, students ride free on all TCAT buses after 6 p.m. weekdays and at any time on weekends
fact_check.note: Page: free after 6 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends.

fact_check.claim: Other students can buy discounted bus passes and OmniRide privileges at myparking.cornell.edu; page gives no prices
fact_check.note: Page says so and points to the 'Purchase a Bus Pass' page on tcatbus.com for prices. tcatbus.com/fares-passes returned 403 for me, so the price could not be checked.

fact_check.claim: Doctoral students and graduate assistants get free OmniRide passes
fact_check.note: Page lists free OmniRide passes for doctoral students and graduate assistants. The Sun column says the same.

fact_check.claim: Short Line takes 15% off a ticket every day of the week for students at eligible colleges
fact_check.note: 15% off, available every day.

fact_check.claim: Trip must start or end in the town on your ID; college picture ID required; one reduced round-trip or one-way ticket per student
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Reduced fares must be bought at a terminal; online purchase available for Cornell and Ithaca College students
fact_check.note: Page says tickets must be bought at a terminal, and that online purchase is available for Cornell, Ithaca College and several other schools. The article's wording is consistent.

fact_check.claim: C2C bus for students with a NetID: $93.50 one way, $187 round trip, including a temporary $6 surcharge
fact_check.note: Matches. The page does not name NYC or give non-student fares, so the article cannot say how much this saves versus the public fare.

fact_check.claim: Cornell says students are eligible for discounted Ithaca Carshare memberships
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Carshare says Cornell helps subsidize annual memberships through the Commuter Alternative Program
fact_check.note: Matches. The page also says the student/commuter rate is $45 off the regular membership, which the article does not use.

fact_check.claim: Just In Case: $30 a year, $9 an hour, 42 cents a mile (cars), for under 6 hours a month
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: It's My Car: $310 a year, $6 an hour, 42 cents a mile, for over 6 hours a month
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: One-time nonrefundable $20 fee per driver per application; sales and rental taxes apply to hourly and mileage charges
fact_check.note: Matches (8% sales tax and 12% special passenger car rental tax).

fact_check.claim: Anabel's Grocery is in Anabel Taylor Hall, opens noon to 7 p.m. Wednesday through Friday and noon to 3 p.m. Saturday, with subsidized prices
fact_check.note: The Sun video (Dec 10, 2024) says this, but a store's hours are a hard fact that rests only on a newspaper page from nearly two years ago. It needs the official Anabel's Grocery page or must be dropped.

fact_check.claim: Anabel's runs during the academic year and accepts SNAP cards
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Nov 10, 2025 update: reduced prices on ten staple items and a 50% discount on groceries for all customers, aimed mainly at people with deep financial need
fact_check.note: The numbers match, but the page says this was an offer made in response to a government shutdown and is dated; it tells readers to check Anabel's site. The article does not say it was a shutdown response, so a reader may take a year-old emergency offer as a standing discount.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Health advice: compare prices across Ithaca stores, rewards and membership programs, generic brands, coupons, check SNAP
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Johnson Museum admission is free for everyone; Tue-Fri 10-5, Sat-Sun noon-4, closed Mondays, closed November 25-27
fact_check.note: Matches. Closure dates are the Thanksgiving closure on the page; the article's 2026 year is implied, so confirm the page is for this year.

fact_check.claim: Free or discounted Cornell Music concerts, Schwartz Center tickets, Cornell Cinema and Cinemapolis tickets; discounted men's hockey tickets
fact_check.note: Page lists these for graduate students. The article flags that the list is graduate-oriented.

fact_check.claim: Big Red Sports Pass gives unlimited access to Cornell sports except men's hockey
fact_check.note: Page says only 'a Big Red Sports Pass for most Cornell sports'. 'Unlimited' and the men's-hockey exception are not in the source.

fact_check.claim: Free equipment loans from Cornell Recreation, open lap swimming at Helen Newman and Teagle, discounted Cornell Outdoor Education classes
fact_check.note: Page lists free sports equipment loans, lap swimming at Helen Newman and Teagle, and discounted outdoor education classes. 'Open' lap swim is not stated but minor.

fact_check.claim: The Cornell Store discounts technology and cell products at its three Ithaca locations
fact_check.note: Page says discounts on technology and cell products at The Cornell Store. 'Three Ithaca locations' is not in the source.

fact_check.claim: In 2014 the Downtown Ithaca Alliance launched a student card: 10, 15 or 20 percent off at 34 businesses for students at Cornell and four other schools
fact_check.note: Matches the October 8, 2014 article, and the article clearly labels it as dated and unconfirmed. Current status unverifiable.

fact_check.claim: Reed Huegerich, Cornell's assistant director of transportation, says nearly a third of students use TCAT as their main way to get to campus
fact_check.note: Matches the guest column; attributed to a named Cornell official.

beats_top.query: how to save money at Cornell student discounts Ithaca
beats_top.why: The #1 result is the Graduate School perks list: official, but written for grad students and with no prices, no TCAT rules after year one, no Carshare plan fees and no Short Line terms. Our page covers undergrads and shows real numbers for Carshare and C2C, but its promise of 'what each saves' is only partly kept: TCAT pass and Short Line fares have no dollar figures, and the C2C fare is not compared to a non-student fare.
changes: Give a dollar figure or a clear 'not published' for each item in the table so 'what each saves' is true, and put the biggest real savings first.
Make the Anabel's section current and officially sourced (hours, whether the 50% offer still runs).
Say plainly which perks are grad-only (OmniRide, perks page items) and which any student gets.

fixes: Change 'Cornell lists first-year undergraduates, graduate and Ph.D. students in their first year, and first-year transfers as eligible' to match the source: 'Fully subsidized passes go to students new to their program, including first-year transfer students'; source https://sustainable.cornell.edu/focus-areas/transportation/bus-commuting

Anabel's hours: replace the noon-7 Wednesday-Friday and noon-3 Saturday hours, which rest only on a December 2024 Cornell Sun video, with hours from Anabel's official Grocery page (find the official site and link it), or delete the hours and say 'see Anabel's website for current hours'.

Anabel's 50% discount: state that the November 10, 2025 offer of reduced prices on ten staples and 50% off for all customers was a response to a government shutdown, that Cornell Health's page dates it and tells readers to check Anabel's site, and that we could not confirm it is still running. Remove 'offers subsidized prices' wording from the intro if the official site does not support it.

Change 'a Big Red Sports Pass for unlimited access to Cornell sports except men's hockey' to 'a Big Red Sports Pass for most Cornell sports'; source https://www.gradschool.cornell.edu/student-experience/student-perks-and-discounts/
Remove 'at its three Ithaca locations' from the Cornell Store sentence; the source only says discounts on technology and cell products at The Cornell Store.

In the Carshare section add that the student and commuter rate is $45 off the regular annual membership for both plans; source https://www.ithacacarshare.org/rates-plans/students-commuters/. Use it in the 'what each saves' table.

Add a note that C2C's student price versus the public fare is not stated on the cited page, or add the public fare from an official Cornell page with a link, so the reader can see what the student rate saves.

Add a short line near the top of the TCAT section stating which TCAT perks are for all students and which (free OmniRide passes) are only for doctoral students and graduate assistants, so undergraduates do not count on them.
